steps.body: Subtracting mixed numbers works the same way — provided the top fraction is big enough to subtract from.
steps.narration: Subtracting mixed numbers works the same way — provided the top fraction is big enough to subtract from.

widget.prompt: Convert 2 3/8 to an improper fraction and build it.
widget.successFeedback: 3/8 is the fraction part; as an improper fraction 2 3/8 is 19 eighths, since each whole is 8.
widget.lowFeedback: That build is SHORTER than 3/8 — either shade more pieces or make each piece larger until the lengths match.
widget.highFeedback: That build is LONGER than 3/8 — either shade fewer pieces or make each piece smaller until the lengths match.

commonFractions.feedback: 8/8 is one whole; the fraction part of 2 3/8 is three eighths.
2/8 reads the whole-number 2 as a numerator; it names the wholes, not the pieces.

predict.prompt: Converting 2 3/8 to eighths, how many pieces?
predict.reveal: Two wholes are sixteen eighths, plus the three already there — 19, not 2 + 3 = 5, which would ignore that each whole is eight eighths.

cml.actionGoal: Rename both fractions to the same piece size, then count the pieces for g5u sub mixed.
invariants: Fractions add and subtract only when their pieces are the same size: renaming scales both parts of a fraction and leaves its value untouched, which is what makes g5u sub mixed a counting problem once the denominators agree.
misconceptions: Adding numerators and denominators across, scaling only one part of a fraction when renaming, or forgetting to trade a whole when the top fraction is too small to subtract from.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: If only the numerators were made equal instead of the denominators, what would go wrong?

widget.prompt: Convert 2 11/12 to an improper fraction. What is the new numerator (over 12)?

commonErrors.feedback: That added the whole to the numerator; each whole is worth 12 pieces, not one.
That converted the wholes but dropped the 11 pieces already in hand.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Give both fractions the same piece size first; after that the pieces simply count.

hints: Trade when the top is short.

The leftover 1 eighths fall short of the 8 needed for another whole.

widget.prompt: Once renamed, 5/6 litre were available and 3/6 litre was poured out. Express what is left as ?/6. What is the numerator?

commonErrors.feedback: That joined the two amounts; pouring out removes pieces rather than adding them.
6 names the piece size, which never changes — only how many are left.
